category_title: Elementary students with ADHD and language delay who improve concentration and social helpfulness through virtual games
scenario_title: Auditory overload and feedback distraction during social interaction
minimal_context: The student is using the voice chat function to practice social interaction with a partner in the 3D virtual zoo.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Let's start the social interaction activity in the virtual zoo. Please use the voice chat to say hello to your partner.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Looks at the screen) The whale is so loud! And there is a dadada sound in the background.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Try to ignore the background sounds and use the voice chat.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Speaks into the headset) Hello? Wait, I can hear my own voice! And I hear the other kids too.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Yes, the voice chat is working. Please continue with the activity.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Starts making loud noises into the microphone) Bzzzz! Ahhhh! (Laughs loudly and completely stops paying attention to the learning activity)

dialogue_combined:
TUTOR: Let's start the social interaction activity in the virtual zoo. Please use the voice chat to say hello to your partner.

STUDENT: (Looks at the screen) The whale is so loud! And there is a dadada sound in the background.

TUTOR: Try to ignore the background sounds and use the voice chat.

STUDENT: (Speaks into the headset) Hello? Wait, I can hear my own voice! And I hear the other kids too.

TUTOR: Yes, the voice chat is working. Please continue with the activity.

STUDENT: (Starts making loud noises into the microphone) Bzzzz! Ahhhh! (Laughs loudly and completely stops paying attention to the learning activity)

context.materials: voice chat function, text chat function, aural and textual feedback, background music/sound, symbol O and X

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: when they found that they could hear their own and others’ voices
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: began to make noises, laugh and totally lose attention to learning activities

behavior_patterns.condition: both aural and textual feedback can easily distract children’s attention from learning if too much information is given
heard the sound of teleport or peak sounds of the whale in the zoo or dadada sound from the background
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: always frightened or very sensitive or always attracted
